batchName: Late Republic: Spartacus and Pompey (78-63 BCE) - Latin words
chapterName: Late Republic: Spartacus and Pompey (78-63 BCE)
description: Written by hand from the chapter text: the Latin words it explains

questions.question: Pompey’s soldiers hailed him as Magnus. What does it mean?
questions.explanation: They named him after Alexander the Great, and he made the name officially his.
questions.sourceQuote: His own soldiers, however, hailed him as "the Great" (*Magnus*), after Alexander the Great

questions.question: Where were about 6,000 captured rebels crucified?
options: Along the Via Appia, the road from Rome to Capua
questions.explanation: Pompey’s troops caught and killed 5,000 more fugitives.
questions.sourceQuote: About 6,000 captured survivors were crucified along the Appian Way (*Via Appia*), the great road from Rome to Capua.

questions.question: Spartacus escaped from one of the ludi at Capua. What were they?
questions.explanation: Prisoners of war and condemned criminals were trained there.
questions.sourceQuote: trained to fight in special schools (*ludi*).

questions.question: What was the decimatio that Crassus revived?
options: Executing one soldier in ten, chosen by lot
A tax of one tenth on plunder
Sending one legion in ten home
questions.explanation: His men learned that Crassus was more dangerous to them than the enemy.
questions.sourceQuote: He revived decimation (*decimatio*), an ancient punishment in which one soldier in every ten was chosen by lot and executed.

questions.question: Pompey skipped the cursus honorum. What was it?
options: The fixed ladder of elected offices
The officer training of the legions
questions.explanation: Normally a Roman climbed it before commanding armies.
questions.sourceQuote: Normally a Roman climbed a fixed ladder of elected offices (*cursus honorum*) before commanding armies.

questions.question: What did the lex Gabinia of 67 BC give Pompey?
options: A three-year command over the provinces near the Mediterranean
questions.explanation: The Senate feared giving one man such power, but the people voted it through.
questions.sourceQuote: proposed the Gabinian Law (*lex Gabinia*) at Pompey's urging.

questions.question: Why was young Pompey called adulescentulus carnifex?
options: For executing a captured former consul
questions.explanation: His own soldiers, by contrast, hailed him as “the Great”.
questions.sourceQuote: His execution of a captured former consul earned him the nickname "teenage butcher" (*adulescentulus carnifex*).

questions.question: Which law of 66 BC handed Pompey the war against Mithridates?
questions.explanation: Lucullus, whom he replaced, called Pompey a vulture who fed on other men’s work.
questions.sourceQuote: In 66 BC a tribune passed the Manilian Law (*lex Manilia*)
